FISHING LICENSES

Fishing license and licence prices by state and country

Buy a fishing licence for the place and water you plan to fish. Your age, residency and trip length determine which option fits. Use the official links below to check exemptions, compare resident prices and find visitor permits. Check extra stamps and access permits before you leave for your trip.

Updated 24 Nov 2026 · By Castward

What should you check before buying a fishing license?

Is there one fishing license for every state and country?

Choose the jurisdiction where you will fish. A home-state licence is not a worldwide pass. Check border-water agreements, the water type and any local permit before you travel. This directory links to the agency for each place.

How much does a fishing licence cost?

The price depends on the place, your residency, age, water type and trip length. The table shows named resident options in their own currencies, not equivalent worldwide packages. For a US holiday, use our separate 3-day, 7-day and annual non-resident comparison.

Where can I buy a fishing license online?

Choose your destination below, then follow its official purchase link. For example, England and Wales uses the government rod-licence service; British Columbia uses WILD for freshwater fishing. Castward compares the rules and sends you to the issuing service; it does not sell licences.

Do children need a fishing licence?

There is no single age rule. In England and Wales, children aged 13 to 16 need a free junior rod licence. B.C. residents under 16 do not need a basic freshwater licence. Check the destination page for the rule that applies to your child and water.

Does a freshwater fishing licence cover the sea or a charter?

Check before you book. Western Australia has a separate powered-boat licence and named activity licences. British Columbia separates freshwater and tidal licences. Charter exemptions also depend on the place, so confirm which licence the operator covers and which permits you must buy yourself.
